title: Observability canary upgrade template + TF & collector playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for doing incremental observability upgrades inside customer VPC/on-prem stacks. Targets: Prometheus + Grafana, OTEL collectors, and log shipping (Fluent Bit / Loki). Mix of TF module notes, smoke-test checklist, rollback signals, and small example configs.

Status / scope: draft brainstorming — not a final runbook. Focus is on minimal blast radius, observable canaries, and TF patterns for safe rollouts.

High-level goals:
- Upgrade OTEL collector to 0.73.x without losing OTLP traffic.
- Migrate Prom scrape jobs to k8s service discovery modules with fewer relabel rules.
- Introduce Loki as optional log retention tier; keep fluent-bit sidecars while we validate throughput.
- Use TF modular approach: network-safe, feature-flagged, and idempotent modules.

Canary strategy (matrix):
- Stage 0 (dry-run): apply TF plan to a non-production namespace (dev) using identical TF variables. Validate plan changes only (no apply).
- Stage 1 (pilot pod group): upgrade OTEL collector as a Deployment in a single availability zone / k8s node-pool. Route 5% of OTLP traffic via weighted k8s service (Envoy / nginx weight) or by altering a routing map in the Collector config.
- Stage 2 (team-wide): expand to 25% of clusters (non-critical clusters). Monitor ingestion rate, latency histograms, dropped spans, and batch size metrics.
- Stage 3 (production): 100% rollout with automatic ramp when SLOs satisfied for 2h.

Key signals to watch (fail fast):
- Prometheus: scrape_count drop > 2% for target job over 5 minutes
- OTEL: span_exporter_errors > 0.1% of spans for 10m
- Latency: p95 export latency increase > 2x baseline
- Logs: backlog in fluent-bit buffer > 10GB (per cluster) or 15min backlog
- Storage: Loki ingestion rate spike > 2x expected causing index pressure
- Alerts: newfatal errors in collector logs, restart_count increase > 3 in 10m

TF module notes / patterns (rough):
- Module layout idea:
  - modules/observability/core (prometheus operator, grafana provisioning)
  - modules/observability/collector (otel-deploy, configmap templates, sidecar injection toggles)
  - modules/observability/logging (fluentbit daemonset, loki-stack optional)
  - modules/observability/ingress (sinks to EL, S3, Kafka egress)

- Inputs (variables): enable_canary boolean, canary_ratio (int), collector_image, loki_enabled boolean, retention_days, storage_backend (s3|block|none)
- Outputs: canary_service_name, prometheus_scrape_targets, grafana_datasources_json_url
- Safety: every module must expose a "preview_only" flag that toggles creation of live sinks; default false. Use preview_only=true when running in staging.
- State: use separate TF state per cluster/namespace. Do not mix pilot and prod into same statefile.

TF snippets to consider (pseudo):
- canary toggle pattern:
  resource "kubernetes_service" "collector_canary" {
    metadata { name = "otel-collector-canary" namespace = var.namespace }
    spec { selector = { app = "otel-collector" } }
  }
  resource "kubernetes_deployment" "collector_canary" { count = var.enable_canary ? 1 : 0 ... }

- immutable config approach: render collector config to ConfigMap with hash annotation and let k8s rollout on change.

OTEL collector config notes (examples / sketch):
- Keep old exporter config as fallback. New config should be behind a receiver alias and a processor that can be switched on via relabeling.
- Sample partial (conceptual):
  receivers:
    otlp/http:
      endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318
  processors:
    batch:
      timeout: 5s
  exporters:
    otlp/primary:
      endpoint: ${BACKEND_OTLP}
    otlp/fallback:
      endpoint: ${OLD_BACKEND}
  service:
    pipelines:
      traces:
        receivers: [otlp/http]
        processors: [batch]
        exporters: [otlp/primary, otlp/fallback]

- Canary routing idea: add a probabilistic sampler or attributes processor to tag 5% of requests and route that tag to a different exporter using the attributes_to_metric or span attributes. Simpler: split traffic via k8s service weights.

Prometheus / scrape plan:
- Move to config templating: build scrape_configs from TF data source ( list of targets ) instead of manual edits.
- Keep a "shadow" Prometheus instance (same config) that scrapes the new targets and writes to a separate remote_write endpoint for validation.
- Scrape interval: preserve existing intervals; for canary use same interval to be comparable.

Grafana / dashboards:
- Provision dashboards via provisioning directory baked into TF. Keep a canary folder: dashboards/canary/* which are only loaded into the canary grafana instance.
- Panel-level validation: ensure dashboard queries have explicit time ranges and minimal cardinality to avoid accidental big queries.

Log shipping / Fluent Bit -> Loki notes:
- Use fluent-bit buffering to filesystem with size-based caps per node. Configure multi-output: primary (loki) + fallback (s3/kafka) to avoid data loss on transient Loki outages.
- Measure ingress by bytes/sec and number of records. For initial canary route only a subset of namespaces to Loki.
- Retention: set loki retention policies using object-storage lifecycle rules.

Smoke-test checklist (pre-apply):
- TF plan has no resources touching production secrets (double-check outputs).
- All modules have preview_only set in staging run.
- Collector config rendered; diffed against existing (kubectl diff).
- Grafana provisioning JSON validates (grafana-cli check).

Smoke-test checklist (post-apply, pilot):
- OTLP success rate > 99.9% for pilot span set
- Prom scrape success rate stable (+/-1%)
- No unexpected restarts on collector pods
- Logs forwarded to Loki for pilot namespaces and queryable within 2m
- Billing / meter: check metric that counts bytes to remote_write for unexpected jump

Rollback plan:
- TF: revert to previous statefile snapshot and apply (document snapshot id)
- Runtime: scale down new collector deployment and flip canary service weight back to 0
- If Loki ingestion overload: switch fluent-bit to fallback (s3) and then resume ingestion slowly after backpressure relieved

Observability validation queries (examples to add to dashboards):
- rate(otel_collector_exporter_sent_spans_total[1m]) grouped by exporter
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(otel_exporter_send_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, exporter))
- prometheus_sd_configs_total - compare target counts before/after

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide standard for backup export: Kafka vs S3 for customers with large log retention requirements
- Should we default to two exporters (primary+fallback) or make fallback opt-in per customer?
- Performance testing: run load generator to validate batch sizes and memory sizing for collector pods (target 2 GB heap limit for 100k spans/sec).
- Terraform module test harness: create a small infra-test pipeline that applies modules in ephemeral GKE/eks/k3s cluster and runs smoke tests automatically.

Appendix: quick commands
- diff collector config: kubectl -n observability get cm otel-config -o yaml > cur.yaml && ./render-config.sh > new.yaml && diff -u cur.yaml new.yaml
- tail collector logs: kubectl -n observability logs -l app=otel-collector -f --tail=200
- check fluent-bit disk buffer usage: kubectl -n logging exec ds/fluent-bit -- df -h /var/log/fluent-bit-buffer

Notes to self: keep TF changes small per PR (one module per PR), include a performance benchmark estimate in PR description, add a checklist to the release manager.

References: add links to customer-specific storage quotas, existing TF modules, and the infra PR that started the upgrade (linked above).

End of draft.
